assignment_statement: Read R and C (1 <= R,C <= 30), followed by an R by C grid whose cells are 0 (open) or 1 (blocked). Count paths from the top-left to the bottom-right using only right and down moves and never entering a blocked cell. If either endpoint is blocked, the answer is zero. Print the path count followed by a newline; it fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

spec_summary: Read R and C (1 <= R,C <= 30), followed by an R by C grid whose cells are 0 (open) or 1 (blocked). control_flow_and_data_types: Uses signed 64-bit integer (long long) for DP table and output.
Loops through rows and columns sequentially.
Conditional logic checks i==0 && j==0 to skip initialization.
Adds contributions from top and left neighbors only.
submission_analysis.implementation_summary: The program reads R, C and a grid of 0s and 1s. It initializes a DP table and iterates to compute paths from top-left to bottom-right, adding contributions from top and left neighbors. It assumes blocked cells are 1 and valid paths are 0.
input_parsing_and_validation: Validates R and C are within [1, 30] and grid values are 0 or 1.
Checks if start (0,0) or end (R-1, C-1) is blocked before processing.
Ensures grid dimensions match input R and C exactly.
Handles malformed input by returning 1 on any validation failure.
likely_weak_points: DP recurrence incorrectly adds paths through blocked cells.
Start/end blocked check only verifies cell value, not path reachability.
Grid dimensions must match input R and C precisely.
No validation for negative R or C values.
Assumes grid is fully populated without bounds checking.
DP initialization sets all cells to 0 instead of blocking start.
